about: The things the event talked about (20-claims/entities.yaml), each with everything the knowledge base links to it. A card is a map, not a source: cite the claim ids it lists; cite holds the citation of each claim.

product.label: Product
product.about: A Google product or service: Search Console, Merchant Center, Discover.

feature.label: Feature
feature.about: A feature of Google Search: AI Mode, AI Overviews, rich results.

crawler.label: Crawler
crawler.about: A crawler or fetcher, named by its user agent: Googlebot, Google-Extended.

report.label: Report
report.about: A report or view of a Google tool: Crawl stats, Page indexing, URL Inspection.

directive.label: Directive
directive.about: A rule a site writes for crawlers or indexing: noindex, rel=canonical, hreflang, Disallow.

status-code.label: Status code
status-code.about: An HTTP status code or class: 404, 429, 5xx.

standard.label: Standard
standard.about: A standard, protocol or format: RFC 9309, HTTP/2, schema.org, JSON-LD.

metric.label: Metric
metric.about: Something measured or budgeted: crawl budget, Core Web Vitals, PageRank.

concept.label: Concept
concept.about: An idea or process: canonicalisation, soft 404, query fan-out, E-E-A-T.

update.label: Update
update.about: A named change to Search: core updates, spam updates, the helpful content update.

tool.label: Tool
tool.about: A testing or research tool: Rich Results Test, Lighthouse, Trends Explore.

is-a.about: The first thing is a kind of the second (404 is-a client error).

part-of.about: The first thing is part of the second (Crawl stats part-of Search Console).

uses.about: The first thing uses the second (AI Mode uses query fan-out).

affects.about: The first thing affects the second (5xx affects the crawl rate).

measured-by.about: The first thing is measured by the second (crawl budget measured-by Crawl stats).

applies-to.about: The first thing applies to the second (hreflang applies-to multilingual sites).

entities.name: AI Mode
entities.summary: Google Search's conversational AI mode for longer questions and follow-ups, answered with query fan-out and grounding on the Search index.
entities.definition: Google Search's AI mode, where users ask longer questions (about three times as long as a traditional search on average, a Google slide said; the opening keynote said two to three times) and follow-up questions. It uses the same crawling and index as Search and adds grounding and query fan-out when it answers.

cite.D1-C193: [D1-C193, press, Relevant Audience (29 September 2026), Google blog (19 May 2026), https://www.relevantaudience.com/seo/google-ai-mode-info-monitoring-global-rollout/]
cite.D2-C729: [D2-C729, docs, Google Search Central, Google blog (5 March 2025), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features]

entities.name: AI Overviews
entities.summary: AI-generated summaries at the top of Google results, with links to the pages that support them.
entities.definition: AI-generated summaries shown in Google results with links to supporting pages. They are built on Google's core ranking systems and use content indexed by Google Search.

cite.D2-C729: [D2-C729, docs, Google Search Central, Google blog (5 March 2025), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features]

entities.name: Allow
entities.summary: The robots.txt rule that lets a crawler fetch a path inside a disallowed one; the most specific matching rule wins.

entities.name: Canonicalization
entities.summary: How Google picks one representative URL (the canonical) from a cluster of duplicate pages and indexes that one.
entities.definition: The representative URL of a duplicate cluster, the one Google would ideally show; signals such as links are forwarded to it.

entities.name: CDN
entities.summary: A content delivery network: servers in front of a site that cache and deliver its pages and files, whose bot protection, firewall rules or throttling can block or slow Google's crawlers.

entities.name: Chrome
entities.summary: Google's web browser; Googlebot renders pages with an up-to-date version of the same Chromium engine, and Chrome's developer tools help debug rendering.

entities.name: Core updates
entities.summary: Broad changes to Google's ranking systems, announced several times a year, that reassess content quality across the web.
entities.definition: A significant, broad change to Google's ranking systems, made several times a year and announced on the Google Search Status Dashboard. Core updates do not target specific sites and are not penalties.

cite.D3-C261: [D3-C261, docs, Google Search Status Dashboard (Ranking incident history), https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history]

entities.name: Crawl budget
entities.summary: The number of URLs Google can and wants to crawl on a site, set by its crawl capacity limit and crawl demand.
entities.definition: How much Google crawls a site: the combination of crawl rate limit and crawl demand, the finite resources Google allocates to crawling one website. A site with fewer than a few thousand URLs likely has no crawl budget problem, Google said.

entities.name: Crawl capacity limit
entities.summary: How much Google can crawl a site without overloading its servers (once called crawl rate limit, internally hostload).
entities.definition: How much crawling a host can take, shared by all Google crawlers. It goes down when connect time, time to first byte, 429 or 5xx responses go up. It applies per host, so a site's CDN, subdomains and main www host may be counted separately. A drop is most of the time an abrupt step down, and Googlebot then opens fewer connections, a Google panelist said.

entities.name: Crawl demand
entities.summary: How much Google wants to crawl a site's URLs, driven by their popularity and how often they change.
entities.definition: How much Google wants to crawl a site, driven by its quality, how often its URLs change and how popular they are. Demand from other Google products, such as Ads, counts too, a Google panelist said.

entities.name: Crawl stats
entities.summary: The Search Console report on Google's crawling of a site: requests, response codes, file types, purpose and host status.
entities.definition: A Search Console report, under Settings, that shows how much Google crawls a site, the responses and errors it received, the file types fetched by its crawlers and the split between discovery of new URLs and refresh of known ones.

entities.name: data-nosnippet
entities.summary: An HTML attribute that keeps a marked part of a page out of Google's snippets.
entities.definition: nosnippet stops text snippets and video previews for a page and keeps its content out of AI Overviews and AI Mode as a direct input; the data-nosnippet attribute hides only a marked part of the page.

entities.name: Disallow
entities.summary: The robots.txt rule that tells a crawler not to fetch the URLs under a path.

cite.D1-C127: [D1-C127, docs, Google Search Central, Search Central blog (10 September 2019), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links]

entities.name: Duplicate content
entities.summary: The same or nearly the same content at several URLs, which Google deduplicates: it clusters the URLs and serves one canonical; not a penalty.
entities.definition: A group of pages Google considers essentially equivalent: it stores one in the index and keeps track of the other URLs.

entities.name: E-E-A-T
entities.summary: Experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness: the qualities Google's rater guidelines ask raters to judge content by.
entities.definition: Experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust, from Google's rater guidelines: first-hand experience, the necessary knowledge or skill, and being a go-to source. Trust comes first: untrustworthy pages have low E-E-A-T however expert they seem.

entities.name: Faceted navigation
entities.summary: Filters such as size, colour or price that create URL variants, which can waste crawl budget when they multiply.
entities.definition: Filters on listing pages whose combinations create very many URLs, for example the same facets in a different order; Google's guide prefers keeping filter URLs from being crawled.

entities.name: Gemini
entities.summary: Google's family of AI models and the assistant app built on them; Gemini models also power AI features in Search and Google Trends.

cite.D3-C094: [D3-C094, docs, Google AI for Developers (Gemini API docs), https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search]

entities.name: Generative AI performance report
entities.summary: Search Console reports that show impressions, pages, countries and dates for a site in Google's generative AI features, without clicks or queries.
entities.definition: Search Console reports, rolled out worldwide by 31 August 2026, that show impressions, pages, countries, devices (Search only) and dates for generative AI features, with no clicks or queries. Since 24 September 2026 they also include multimodal searches; the regular Performance report still counts AI traffic too.

entities.name: GEO
entities.summary: Generative engine optimisation (and its twin AEO): labels for optimising for AI answers, which Google says good SEO already covers.
entities.definition: Labels for generative engine optimisation and answer engine optimisation. Google's answer: don't worry about the name, good SEO is good GEO and AEO.

entities.name: Discover
entities.summary: Google's personalised feed of articles and videos, shown without a query, with its own report in Search Console.
entities.definition: Google's Discover surface: indexed content that meets Discover's content policies is eligible automatically, with no special tags or structured data, and Discover uses many of the same signals and systems as Search.

entities.name: Google-Extended
entities.summary: A robots.txt control token, not a separate crawler, that decides whether crawled content may be used for Gemini models and grounding outside Search.
entities.definition: A robots.txt control token, not a separate crawler, that decides whether crawled content may train future Gemini models and ground Gemini apps and Vertex AI. It does not affect inclusion or ranking in Google Search. A site can disallow it for a directory or for the whole site.

entities.name: Google Images
entities.summary: Google's image search, which shows images from the web with a link to the page that hosts them.

entities.name: Google Lens
entities.summary: Google's visual search: search with a photo or a part of the screen instead of typed words.
entities.definition: Google's visual search, which Google said it built after seeing young users upload pictures and expect answers about them; more than 1.5 billion people use it every month, according to Google's May 2025 announcement.

entities.name: Search Console
entities.summary: Google's free tool that reports how a site does in Search: indexing, crawling, performance and enhancements.

cite.D1-C266: [D1-C266, docs, Google Search Console API documentation, https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/prereqs]
cite.D3-C473: [D3-C473, docs, Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/11/search-console-branded-filter]
cite.D3-C499: [D3-C499, docs, Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/11/search-console-branded-filter]
cite.D3-C667: [D3-C667, docs, Google Search Central, Google Search Console Help, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/submit-updated-robots-txt]

entities.name: Google Shopping
entities.summary: Google's shopping results and the Shopping tab, built from Merchant Center feeds and product markup.

entities.name: Google Trends
entities.summary: Google's free tool that shows how search interest in a term or topic changes over time and across places, as a share of all searches.

cite.D2-C767: [D2-C767, docs, Google blog (14 August 2024), Google Trends Help, https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/google-trends-trending-now-update/]

entities.name: Googlebot
entities.summary: Google Search's main crawler, which fetches pages for the index as a smartphone or desktop user agent.

cite.D2-C206: [D2-C206, docs, Search Central blog (3 December 2024), Search Central blog (31 March 2026), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-resources]

entities.name: Grounding
entities.summary: Giving an AI model content from the Search index at answer time, so that its answer rests on that content.
entities.definition: Giving an AI model content from the Google Search index at prompt time, so that its answer rests on that content.

cite.D3-C094: [D3-C094, docs, Google AI for Developers (Gemini API docs), https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search]

entities.name: hreflang
entities.summary: Annotations that tell Google which language or regional versions of a page exist, so it can show the right one to each user.
entities.definition: Annotations that tell Google which pages are language or regional versions of each other, so it can show the right one. They do not set a page's language.

entities.summary: The HTTP status code for success: the server returns the page, and its content can be considered for indexing.
The HTTP status code for a forbidden request; to Googlebot it is a client error and does not slow crawling the way 429 does.
The HTTP status code for a page that does not exist; Google drops such URLs from the index and crawls them less often.
The HTTP status code for a page that is gone for good; Google treats it much like a 404.
The HTTP status code for too many requests; Google treats it like a server error and slows crawling.

entities.name: 4xx
entities.summary: The class of HTTP status codes for client errors; apart from 429 they do not slow Google's crawling.
entities.definition: 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error and 5xx server error. Each class affects crawling differently, and 429 is the 4xx code that tells Google to slow down instead of saying there is nothing at the URL.

entities.summary: The HTTP status code for a temporarily unavailable server, the right answer for planned maintenance and short outages.

entities.name: 5xx
entities.summary: The class of HTTP status codes for server errors; Google slows crawling when it sees them and drops URLs that keep returning them.
entities.definition: 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error and 5xx server error. Each class affects crawling differently, and 429 is the 4xx code that tells Google to slow down instead of saying there is nothing at the URL.

entities.name: Index selection
entities.summary: Google's decision whether a crawled and processed page is worth keeping in the index.
entities.definition: The last step before Google's index: it calculates thresholds and decides which documents are kept, using the signals calculated earlier, such as quality, language, country and spam.

entities.name: JavaScript
entities.summary: The web's scripting language; Google renders JavaScript before indexing, but content and links that need it are at risk.

cite.D2-C206: [D2-C206, docs, Search Central blog (3 December 2024), Search Central blog (31 March 2026), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-resources]

entities.name: JSON-LD
entities.summary: The JSON-based format for structured data that Google recommends.
entities.definition: The structured data syntax Google recommends: one contiguous block that is easier to write correctly. Microdata and RDFa are interpreted the same way.

entities.name: Lazy loading
entities.summary: Loading images or content only when they come into view; Google sees it only if it works without scrolling or clicks.
entities.definition: Loading content only when it is needed. Triggered by an Intersection Observer it can work for Google; triggered by scroll events or clicks it does not.

entities.name: llms.txt
entities.summary: A proposed text file that lists a site's content for AI systems; Google Search does not use it.
entities.definition: A text file some sites add for AI systems. Google says it isn't necessary: Google Search ignores such AI text files, so they neither help nor harm. On Day 1 Google said llms.txt does not matter for Google Search right now and that it does not expect it to.

entities.name: Main content
entities.summary: The part of a page that serves its purpose, which Google identifies and weighs more than boilerplate such as navigation.
entities.definition: The part of a page that serves its purpose, as opposed to header, navigation and footer: any part that directly helps the page achieve its purpose, including images, video, tools and user-generated content. Google identifies it and treats it as the most important part of the page.

cite.D2-C870: [D2-C870, docs, Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (PDF, 11 September 2025), https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf]
cite.D2-C871: [D2-C871, docs, Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (PDF, 11 September 2025), https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf]

entities.name: max-image-preview
entities.summary: A robots rule that sets the largest image preview Google may show for a page: none, standard or large.
entities.definition: A robots rule for the largest image preview Google may show: none, standard or large, for example in Discover.

entities.name: max-snippet
entities.summary: A robots rule that caps the length of a page's text snippet in Google results, in characters.
entities.definition: A robots rule that caps a snippet at a number of characters: 0 means no snippet and -1 means no limit. It also limits how much of the page AI features may use.

entities.name: Merchant Center
entities.summary: Google's tool where retailers submit product data (feeds) that Google Shopping, free listings and AI shopping experiences use.
entities.definition: Google's tool through which merchants send product data feeds for Shopping ads, Search ads and organic results. Products need it to appear in the Shopping tab; product rich results do not.

entities.name: Robots meta tag
entities.summary: A meta tag in a page's HTML that gives search engines page-level rules such as noindex, nofollow or nosnippet.
entities.definition: An HTML tag in the head of a page that gives search engines page-specific rules, such as noindex or nosnippet, for indexing and display in results.

entities.name: nofollow
entities.summary: A rule, on a whole page or on one link (rel=nofollow), that asks Google not to follow links; Google treats it as a hint.
entities.definition: A hint not to follow links or pass signals through them; as a page-level robots rule it covers every link on the page. It does not block crawling.

cite.D1-C127: [D1-C127, docs, Google Search Central, Search Central blog (10 September 2019), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links]

entities.name: noindex
entities.summary: A robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag rule that tells Google not to show a page in search results.
entities.definition: A robots rule that tells Google not to show a page in search results. It works only if Google can crawl the page and see the rule.

entities.name: nosnippet
entities.summary: A robots rule that stops Google from showing a text snippet or video preview for a page, also as input to AI Overviews and AI Mode.
entities.definition: nosnippet stops text snippets and video previews for a page and keeps its content out of AI Overviews and AI Mode as a direct input; the data-nosnippet attribute hides only a marked part of the page.

entities.name: notranslate
entities.summary: A meta tag value and HTML class that stops Google from offering a translation of a page or of part of it.

entities.name: Page indexing report
entities.summary: The Search Console report that lists which URLs are indexed and why the others are not.

entities.name: PageRank
entities.summary: Google's original link-based ranking algorithm, from the BackRub research project at Stanford.
entities.definition: PageRank is the link-analysis algorithm Google's founders invented; BackRub was their 1995 Stanford search engine, soon renamed Google. Google's ranking systems guide says PageRank has evolved and is still part of its core ranking systems.

entities.name: Performance report
entities.summary: The Search Console report of clicks, impressions, click-through rate and position for a site's queries and pages.

entities.name: Platform properties
entities.summary: Search Console properties for a site's social and video platform channels, showing how that content performs in Google Search.
entities.definition: Search Console properties for Instagram, TikTok, X or YouTube accounts, verified through a pop-up from the platform, that show how the account's content performs on Google Search, Discover and Google News.

entities.name: Query fan-out
entities.summary: Running several related searches at once to gather material for an AI answer, as AI Mode and AI Overviews do.
entities.definition: Running several related searches at once to gather more results for an AI answer; a question about lawn weeds may also search herbicides and weed prevention. In Google's AI features an LLM generates the fan-out queries, and each goes through the same query understanding as a typed query; Google said they are not added to Search Console.

cite.D2-C729: [D2-C729, docs, Google Search Central, Google blog (5 March 2025), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features]

entities.name: Query groups
entities.summary: A Search Console Insights feature that groups similar queries together so their clicks can be read as one topic.
entities.definition: Search Console groups of queries with very similar intent written differently, computed with AI and titled with the most prominent query. Shown in Search Console Insights for properties with many queries; they do not affect ranking.

entities.name: Query understanding
entities.summary: How Google interprets a query (spelling, synonyms, language, intent) before it retrieves results.
entities.definition: The first serving step: Google detects a query's language, separates its words, drops stop words where they matter little, recognises entities and expands the query with synonyms before looking it up. Google said it rewrites pretty much every query.

entities.name: Redirects
entities.summary: Answers that send crawlers and users from one URL to another, server-side (permanent 301 and 308, temporary 302 and 307) or with JavaScript; a strong canonical signal and the core of a site move.

entities.name: rel=canonical
entities.summary: A link element that names the preferred URL among duplicates; one of several signals Google weighs when it picks the canonical.
entities.definition: A link element in the head of a page that names the site owner's preferred URL. Google treats it as a strong signal, not an order.

entities.name: Rendering
entities.summary: Running a page's JavaScript in a headless Chrome so Google sees the content as a browser shows it.
entities.definition: Running a page's JavaScript in a browser engine to see what users see. Google renders with Chromium and indexes the rendered HTML.

cite.D2-C200: [D2-C200, docs, Google Search Central (SEO office hours transcript, March 2023), https://developers.google.com/search/help/office-hours/2023/march]
cite.D2-C206: [D2-C206, docs, Search Central blog (3 December 2024), Search Central blog (31 March 2026), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-resources]
cite.D2-C273: [D2-C273, docs, Google Search Central (SEO office hours transcript, March 2023), https://developers.google.com/search/help/office-hours/2023/march]

entities.name: Rich results
entities.summary: Search results with extra visual features, such as ratings, prices or images, that structured data can make a page eligible for.
entities.definition: Search results with extra visual features, such as review stars or recipe filters, usually powered by structured data. AI Overviews and AI Mode are not rich results.

entities.name: Rich Results Test
entities.summary: Google's tool that tests a page or code snippet for structured data that can produce rich results.
entities.definition: Google's tool to test and preview structured data: it shows the rich result features it detected and whether the markup is valid. It tests either a URL or a pasted code snippet.

entities.name: robots.txt
entities.summary: The text file at the root of a host that tells crawlers which paths they may fetch, standardised by the IETF in 2022 as the Robots Exclusion Protocol (RFC 9309).
entities.definition: A file in the root of each host (example.com/robots.txt) that tells crawlers which URLs they may fetch. It controls crawling, not indexing, applies only to its own host and is not a security measure: anyone can read it.

cite.D1-C127: [D1-C127, docs, Google Search Central, Search Central blog (10 September 2019), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links]
cite.D3-C667: [D3-C667, docs, Google Search Central, Google Search Console Help, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/submit-updated-robots-txt]

entities.name: robots.txt report
entities.summary: The Search Console report that shows the robots.txt files Google found for a site, when it fetched them and any parsing errors.
entities.definition: A Search Console report that shows the robots.txt file as Google last fetched it, with a version history and the errors and successes of each fetch. Google said it uses Google's open-source robots.txt parser.

cite.D3-C667: [D3-C667, docs, Google Search Central, Google Search Console Help, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/submit-updated-robots-txt]

entities.name: Scaled content abuse
entities.summary: The spam policy against producing many pages mainly to manipulate rankings, whether by AI, people or both.
entities.definition: A Google spam policy against generating many pages mainly to manipulate rankings with little value to users, however they are made, including automated translation of scraped content.

entities.name: Schema.org
entities.summary: The shared vocabulary of types and properties that structured data uses, launched by the major search engines in 2011.
entities.definition: The shared markup vocabulary that major search engines announced together in June 2011; Google uses only the subsets its documentation declares.

entities.name: Search Console API
entities.summary: The programming interface for reading Search Console data, such as performance and URL inspection, outside the web interface.

cite.D1-C266: [D1-C266, docs, Google Search Console API documentation, https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/prereqs]
cite.D1-C267: [D1-C267, docs, Google Search Console API documentation, https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/pricing]

entities.name: Search generative AI control
entities.summary: A Search Console property setting (inherit, include or exclude) that controls whether a site appears in Google's generative AI features without changing its web rankings.
entities.definition: A Search Console property setting (inherit, include or exclude) that controls whether a site appears in AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI features in Discover, without affecting web rankings.

entities.name: Search interest
entities.summary: Google Trends' measure: searches for a term as a share of all searches at a time and place, scaled 0 to 100.
entities.definition: Google Trends' measure: the share of all searches for a term, on a 0 to 100 scale. It is not search volume.

entities.name: Search profiles
entities.summary: A profile in Google Search where publishers and creators show their work and channels in one place.
entities.definition: A profile publishers and creators can claim in Google Search, with name, photo, bio, links and pinned posts, which users can follow. In the US, 10,000 followers across YouTube, Instagram, X or TikTok qualify since 16 September 2026. Its verified accounts are added automatically as Search Console platform properties.

entities.name: Search quality raters
entities.summary: People who rate the quality of Google's results against published guidelines; their ratings test changes and do not rank pages.
entities.definition: External reviewers who rate results for changes Google is testing, following the Search Quality Rater Guidelines. They cannot affect individual sites' rankings, and nothing in their guidelines is itself a ranking factor.

cite.D2-C870: [D2-C870, docs, Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (PDF, 11 September 2025), https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf]
cite.D2-C871: [D2-C871, docs, Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (PDF, 11 September 2025), https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf]
cite.D3-C710: [D3-C710, docs, Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (PDF, 11 September 2025), https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf]
cite.D3-C711: [D3-C711, docs, Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (PDF, 11 September 2025), https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf]

entities.name: Single-page app
entities.summary: A website that loads one page and swaps content with JavaScript, which needs real URLs and status codes to be indexed well.
entities.definition: A JavaScript application that changes views without full page reloads. Typical search risks: links without real URLs, # routes and error views that return 200.

entities.name: Site move
entities.summary: Moving a site to new URLs or a new domain, with redirects and Search Console's Change of Address tool.

entities.name: Sitemaps
entities.summary: Files that list a site's URLs (with optional last-modified dates) so search engines can discover them.

cite.D1-C127: [D1-C127, docs, Google Search Central, Search Central blog (10 September 2019), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links]

entities.name: Snippets
entities.summary: The text under a result's title link, which Google creates automatically from the page's content and which robots rules such as nosnippet and max-snippet can limit.

entities.name: Soft 404
entities.summary: A page that tells users it does not exist (or is empty) but answers with 200; Google treats it as an error and drops it.
entities.definition: A page that returns a success code (200) while its content looks like an error or an empty page. Google keeps it out of the index but may keep crawling it. A CDN captcha page served with 200 is a common cause.

entities.name: Spam updates
entities.summary: Updates to Google's spam-detection systems, announced on the Search Status Dashboard.
entities.definition: A notable improvement to Google's automated spam detection systems, such as SpamBrain, listed with its ranking updates. Spam updates target spam pages; to recover, a site removes the spam Google described.

cite.D3-C202: [D3-C202, docs, Google Search Status Dashboard (Ranking incident history), Google Search Status Dashboard (September 2026 spam update), https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history]
cite.D3-C261: [D3-C261, docs, Google Search Status Dashboard (Ranking incident history), https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history]

entities.name: SpamBrain
entities.summary: Google's AI-based spam-prevention system.
entities.definition: Google's AI-based spam prevention system, launched in 2018 and continuously improved since; Google said it is now built on Gemini.

entities.name: Special-case crawlers
entities.summary: Google crawlers for specific products under an agreement with the site (such as AdsBot), which may ignore the global robots.txt user agent.
entities.definition: Google crawlers that serve a specific product by agreement with the crawled site, and the only Google crawlers that may ignore robots.txt; AdsBot, for example, ignores the global user agent with the ad publisher's permission.

entities.name: Storebot-Google
entities.summary: Google's crawler for shopping pages, which checks product pages, prices and checkout for Google Shopping.
entities.definition: Google Shopping's own crawler. It crawls more often than Googlebot, goes through product, cart and checkout pages to verify merchant data, and robots.txt rules for it affect all Google Shopping surfaces.

entities.name: Structured data
entities.summary: Machine-readable markup, usually Schema.org in JSON-LD, that describes a page's content and can make it eligible for rich results.
entities.definition: Machine-readable markup that describes a page's content, so Google understands it more accurately and the page can become eligible for rich results.

entities.name: Tokenization
entities.summary: Splitting text into tokens (words or word parts) for the index or for an AI model.
entities.definition: Splitting text into small units. Google Search stores words (tokens) with metadata, while AI models split text into sub-word pieces mapped to numeric IDs.

entities.name: Trending now
entities.summary: The Google Trends page that lists searches rising fast right now, by country and category.
entities.definition: The Google Trends tab that shows what people are searching for on Google right now, with approximate, bucketed search volumes.

cite.D2-C767: [D2-C767, docs, Google blog (14 August 2024), Google Trends Help, https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/google-trends-trending-now-update/]
cite.D2-C768: [D2-C768, docs, Google Trends Help, Google Search Central, https://support.google.com/trends/answer/3076011?hl=en]

entities.name: Trends Explore
entities.summary: The Google Trends page for comparing search terms and topics over time, by region and with related queries.

entities.name: URL Inspection
entities.summary: The Search Console tool that shows how Google sees one URL: index status, the chosen canonical, and a live test with the rendered HTML.
entities.definition: Search Console's tool that shows how Google sees a URL, including the rendered HTML; its live test can differ from the indexed version.

entities.name: User-triggered fetchers
entities.summary: Google fetchers that request a page because a user asked for it (for example a site verification), and that generally ignore robots.txt.
entities.definition: Fetchers that request a page because a user asked for it, such as a translation service. Google's documentation says they generally ignore robots.txt, and Google said AI agents acting for a user fall into the same category.

entities.name: WebMCP
entities.summary: A proposed web standard that lets a page expose its actions as tools that AI agents in the browser can call.
entities.definition: Web Model Context Protocol: a proposed web standard that lets a site declare the actions it offers AI agents, through declarative HTML annotations or imperative tools. Chrome offers it for testing through an origin trial or a flag.

entities.name: X-Robots-Tag
entities.summary: An HTTP response header that carries robots rules such as noindex, so they also work for PDFs, images and other non-HTML files.
entities.definition: An HTTP header that carries the same rules as the robots meta tag, also for files that are not HTML. Like the tag, Google only sees it on URLs it is allowed to crawl.

entities.name: YouTube
entities.summary: Google's video platform; its videos appear in Search, and channels can be added to Search Console as platform properties.
